name: Neural Disruption Pistol NDP-4 'Stutter'
description:
The NDP-4 fires a dart-delivered neural feedback payload: a 2mm tungsten needle carrying a microscale piezoelectric transceiver and a burst-charge of neurotransmitter-disrupting polymer gel. On impact — typically at ranges under 40 meters — the needle embeds in soft tissue and the piezoelectric element activates from the kinetic impact, generating a localized electrical field that destabilizes sodium-channel gating in nearby motor neurons. The polymer gel simultaneously releases a fast-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor into the surrounding tissue, creating a 3-6 second window of profound motor disruption — the target experiences inability to initiate voluntary movement while remaining fully conscious. The effect is colloquially described as 'being frozen mid-thought.'

The NDP-4 uses a neural feedback loop architecture originally developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS for surgical tremor suppression. In its weapons application, the same feedback principle that once stabilized a surgeon's hands is inverted: the transceiver reads the target's local neural activity and generates counter-phase interference signals that scramble motor command transmission. This active interference component extends the disruption window beyond what the chemical payload alone would produce, and means the effect duration varies with the target's neural architecture — individuals with cybernetic motor augmentation may experience shorter disruption (1-2 seconds) or, in documented cases, a paradoxical amplification effect where the augmentation systems attempt to compensate and produce involuntary movement cascades instead.

The pistol itself is compact and conventionally shaped, operating on a CO2-driven dart projector with a 6-round rotary cylinder. Each dart is individually sealed in a nitrogen-purged capsule to preserve the polymer gel payload. The weapon produces minimal sound — a soft pneumatic pop — and no visible projectile, which has made it a favorite of abduction and interrogation specialists who need a target incapacitated without permanent damage and without witnesses understanding what just happened.
specifications: caliber: 2mm tungsten neural-payload dart feed system: 6-round rotary cylinder, nitrogen-sealed dart capsules propulsion: CO2 pneumatic, 12g standard cartridge (18 shots) effective range: 5-40m optimal, degraded accuracy beyond 40m disruption duration: 3-6 seconds (baseline), 1-2 seconds (augmented targets), variable (heavy augmentation) weight: 0.7 kg loaded dimensions: 220mm length, 135mm height acoustic signature: ~62 dB (comparable to a book dropped on a hard floor) contraindications: Unpredictable in targets with Tier 3+ motor augmentation; potentially lethal with cardiac neural implants
tactical_use: The NDP-4 is almost exclusively used for non-lethal incapacitation in abduction, extraction, and interrogation scenarios. A single dart creates a 3-6 second window during which a target can be physically controlled without resistance. Operators typically work in pairs — one fires the NDP-4 while the second moves immediately to physically secure the target, who will be conscious, aware, and terrified but unable to resist. The 6-round cylinder allows for multiple targets in sequence. Experienced operators carry a secondary conventional firearm for situations where the target proves augmented or where the disruption window is insufficient.
cultural_context: The NDP-4 occupies a particularly feared niche in GLMZ's criminal ecosystem because it is understood as a kidnapper's weapon. Its presence at a scene tells investigators that the perpetrators wanted someone alive and mobile — they needed the target incapacitated for seconds, not dead. The weapon is associated with corporate abduction teams, organ-trafficking operations, and political disappearances. Among the city's augmented population, the NDP-4 carries additional dread because of documented cases where heavy motor augmentation caused the 'amplification effect' — victims with full-body cybernetic systems have experienced violent involuntary convulsions lasting minutes rather than seconds of frozen stillness. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS has publicly disavowed any weapons application of their neural feedback research, a statement that has been received with widespread skepticism.
story_hooks: A recovered NDP-4 dart from a disappearance scene carries a HELIX BIOSYSTEMS batch code that traces to a research division officially shut down two years ago — someone is still manufacturing

A target with Tier 4 motor augmentation experienced the amplification effect and died from the convulsive response — the operator who fired the dart is now being hunted by their own employer to eliminate the witness

Someone is using NDP-4s to abduct low-tier arcology residents who have no augmentation and no one looking for them — the pattern of disappearances only becomes visible when someone starts mapping them
A player character is hit by an NDP-4 dart and experiences the 3-6 second disruption while fully conscious during a critical moment — and sees something they were not meant to see

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, clinical pistol with an almost medical aesthetic—compact and purposeful, designed to disappear into a tactical rig. The profile suggests precision and restraint rather than raw power. The rotary cylinder is the dominant visual feature, sitting proud of the grip like a surgical instrument's chamber.
physical_description.dimensions: 220mm length, 135mm height, approximately 35mm width at widest point (cylinder). Barrel stub approximately 60mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Distinctly light—0.7 kg loaded feels almost toy-like in hand, which belies its function. The balance tips slightly forward toward the barrel, encouraging controlled aim. Handled with the weight of a high-end airsoft replica, but with denser, more precise construction.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite body with titanium-alloy internal mechanisms. The rotary cylinder is hardened stainless steel to contain pressurized nitrogen capsules.
physical_description.finish: Matte forensic black on the polymer frame, contrasting with brushed surgical-steel accents around the cylinder release and trigger housing. The cylinder itself bears a subtle iridescence where light catches the precision-machined grooves.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black with brushed steel/titanium accents. Faint cyan accent lighting around the CO2 cartridge chamber indicator—a small LED that pulses to show remaining shots.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured medical-grade polymer with gentle ergonomic contouring—not aggressive, but firmly grippy. Barely any stippling; it feels designed for precision and control rather than combat aggression. Cool to the touch.
distinctive_features: Six-round rotary cylinder with individual nitrogen-sealed capsule wells, each marked with a micro-etched dart status indicator
Tiny cyan LED pulse indicator on the lower receiver showing CO2 charge level
Aperture sight with tritium inlays for low-light targeting
CO2 cartridge window on the left side showing remaining propellant pressure gauge
Integrated safety lever that glows faintly when armed
Serial micro-etchings along the frame—minimalist manufacturer stamps
Minimal texture on the muzzle brake—just the smallest ports for CO2 venting
A small ejector pin on the cylinder that gently pops spent capsules sideways, leaving no brass
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (a double helix wrapped around a stylized neural synapse) etched subtly into the left side of the frame at mid-length. Serial number in micro-font on the right side of the cylinder hub. No aggressive branding—this is a black-market weapon; discretion is built in.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field specimens range from pristine (recently stolen from corpo armory) to well-maintained but subtly worn. Operators obsessively care for the nitrogen-sealed cylinder mechanism, so cosmetic wear is common while mechanical wear is rare. Some veteran examples show faint finger oils on the grip and microscratches around the cylinder from rapid reloads. Rarely battle-scarred—this weapon is used in planned extractions, not firefights.
